title: Should we talk about our salaries
titleChinese: 同事之间工资应该公开吗？
paragraphs: It's a touchy subject. Talking socially about money can make people feel uncomfortable. But at work, have a conversation about how much people earn, and things can not only get awkward, but, in some cases, it can get you sacked.

According to a survey by the Trades Union Congress, 1 in 5 workers "have been told they can’t talk about their pay at work". This, concludes the TUC, indicates how common pay secrecy or 'gagging' clauses are in employment contracts. 'Pay secrecy clauses are a get out of jail free card for bad bosses,' said TUC general secretary Frances O'Grady. 'They stop workers from challenging unfair pay, allow top executives to hoard profits and encourage discrimination. More openness about wages is essential to building fairer workplaces.'

So, should we talk about how much we earn? It's not so simple. Even without the contractual obligations, people may still be reluctant. "I personally have found it's better not looking and not knowing," Tracy Jordan, an HR professional, told the BBC. "Even if you feel you are paid a fair wage, there will always be someone that you perceive is doing a lesser job and is earning more. Rather than feeling perpetually dissatisfied, I think ignorance can be bliss."

Money is tied up with complex emotions, Brianna McGurran, a money expert at the personal finance blog NerdWallet, told the New York Times. It involves emotions like shame, success and fear of failure. It also influences how people view you. People's money is tied to their self-worth. As a result, culturally, it can be bit of a taboo.

But all that may change. First of all, pay secrecy clauses are unenforceable in the UK due to the UK Equality Act 2010. An employee must always be able to find out if they are being discriminated against in terms of pay. In addition, The European Union is considering new legislation on pay transparency in order to reduce gender pay, earnings and pension gaps. So, for better or worse it may be something we all have to get used to. Over time, talking about our salaries may become just another matter for small talk.

vocabulary.entry: touchy /ˈtʌtʃi/ adj. 敏感的；棘手的
vocabulary.example: Religion is always a touchy subject when we're with my relatives.
vocabulary.translation: 和亲戚相处时，宗教总是个敏感话题。

vocabulary.entry: sacked /sækt/ adj. 被解雇的
vocabulary.example: He was sacked from his job after arguing with the manager.
vocabulary.translation: 他和经理争吵后被解雇了。

vocabulary.entry: pay secrecy /ˈpeɪ ˈsiːkrəsi/ 薪资保密
vocabulary.example: Pay secrecy is still common in many traditional companies.
vocabulary.translation: 薪资保密在许多传统公司里依然很常见。

vocabulary.entry: gagging clause /ˈɡæɡɪŋ klɔːz/ 封口条款
vocabulary.example: The contract included a gagging clause preventing her from talking to the press.
vocabulary.translation: 这份合同包含一项封口条款，禁止她向媒体透露消息。

vocabulary.entry: employment contract /ɪmˈplɔɪmənt ˈkɒntrækt/ 雇佣合同
vocabulary.example: You should read the small print in your employment contract carefully.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该仔细阅读雇佣合同中的附属细则。

vocabulary.term: get out of jail free card
vocabulary.entry: get out of jail free card /ɡet aʊt ɒv dʒeɪl friː kɑːd/ 免罪符；脱身妙计
vocabulary.example: The politician used his connection as a get out of jail free card.
vocabulary.translation: 这位政客把自己的人脉当作了脱身妙计。

vocabulary.entry: hoard /hɔːd/ v. 囤积；积聚
vocabulary.example: The company has been accused of hoarding profits instead of raising wages.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司被指控囤积利润，而非给员工涨薪。

vocabulary.entry: discrimination /dɪˌskrɪmɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 歧视；区别对待
vocabulary.example: The law prohibits discrimination on the grounds of age or gender.
vocabulary.translation: 这项法律禁止基于年龄或性别的歧视行为。

vocabulary.entry: contractual obligation /kənˈtræktʃuəl ˌɒblɪˈɡeɪʃn/ 合同义务
vocabulary.example: The company failed to meet its contractual obligations to deliver the goods on time.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司未能履行按时交货的合同义务。

vocabulary.entry: reluctant /rɪˈlʌktənt/ adj. 不情愿的；勉强的
vocabulary.example: She was reluctant to admit that she had made a mistake.
vocabulary.translation: 她不情愿承认自己犯了错。

vocabulary.entry: perceive /pəˈsiːv/ v. 认为；看待
vocabulary.example: He perceived himself as a victim of the system.
vocabulary.translation: 他把自己看作是这个制度的受害者。

vocabulary.entry: perpetually /pəˈpetʃuəli/ adv. 永恒地；持续不断地
vocabulary.example: The office is perpetually cold in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 这间办公室冬天总是冷冰冰的。

vocabulary.entry: ignorance is bliss /ˈɪɡnərəns ɪz blɪs/ 无知是福
vocabulary.example: I don't want to know the details of their argument—ignorance is bliss.
vocabulary.translation: 我不想知道他们争吵的细节——无知是福。

vocabulary.entry: self-worth /ˌself ˈwɜːθ/ n. 自我价值
vocabulary.example: Her self-worth was closely tied to her professional achievements.
vocabulary.translation: 她的自我价值与职业成就紧密相连。

vocabulary.entry: taboo /təˈbuː/ n. 禁忌；忌讳
vocabulary.example: In some cultures, it's a taboo to mention death in daily conversation.
vocabulary.translation: 在一些文化中，日常对话里提及死亡是一种禁忌。

vocabulary.entry: unenforceable /ˌʌnɪnˈfɔːsəbl/ adj. 无法强制执行的
vocabulary.example: The agreement was declared unenforceable by the court.
vocabulary.translation: 这份协议被法院判定为无法强制执行。

vocabulary.entry: Equality Act /iˈkwɒləti ækt/ 平等法案
vocabulary.example: The Equality Act was introduced to protect people from unfair treatment.
vocabulary.translation: 平等法案的出台是为了保护人们免受不公平待遇。

vocabulary.entry: discriminate /dɪˈskrɪmɪneɪt/ v. 歧视；区别对待
vocabulary.example: It is illegal to discriminate against employees on the basis of race.
vocabulary.translation: 基于种族歧视员工是违法行为。

vocabulary.entry: pay transparency /ˈpeɪ trænsˈpærənsi/ 薪资透明度
vocabulary.example: Pay transparency can help reduce the gender pay gap in the workplace.
vocabulary.translation: 薪资透明度有助于缩小职场中的性别薪酬差距。

vocabulary.entry: gender pay gap /ˈdʒendə ˈpeɪ ɡæp/ 性别薪酬差距
vocabulary.example: The company is taking steps to close the gender pay gap.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司正在采取措施缩小性别薪酬差距。

vocabulary.entry: pension gap /ˈpenʃn ɡæp/ 养老金差距
vocabulary.example: The government has proposed new policies to address the pension gap.
vocabulary.translation: 政府提出了新政策来解决养老金差距问题。

vocabulary.entry: small talk /ˌsmɔːl ˈtɔːk/ 闲聊；寒暄
vocabulary.example: We made small talk about the weather while waiting for the bus.
vocabulary.translation: 等公交车时，我们聊了聊天气之类的闲话。
